The '''2014–15 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga NOS''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 81st season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. It began on 15 August 2014 and concluded on 23 May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Primeira Liga|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/37495/calendario-primeira-liga-2014-2015.pdf|format=PDF|work=Liga Portugal.pt|publisher=[[Portuguese League for Professional Football]] (LPFP)|access-date=5 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205195821/http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/37495/calendario-primeira-liga-2014-2015.pdf|archive-date=2015-02-05|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 17 May 2015, [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] won their second consecutive and 34th overall title.

==Events==
The league was scaled up to 18 teams, after the Court's rule to nullify [[Boavista F.C.|Boavista]]'s relegation from the Primeira Liga in the [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|2007–08 season]]. Boavista has been invited back in the Primeira Liga, after the club won a legal battle that eventually deemed their forced relegation five years ago unlawful. The club therefore went straight from the third level to the top league.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.theportugalnews.com/news/boavista-back-in-the-top-flight/28255 | title=Boavista back in the top flight | publisher=theportugalnews.com | date=18 April 2013 | access-date=10 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190604043540/https://www.theportugalnews.com/news/boavista-back-in-the-top-flight/28255 | archive-date=4 June 2019 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://portugoal.info/index.php/more-liga-sagres-news/40396-boavista-back-in-the-top-flight | title=Boavista back in the top flight in 2013/14 | publisher=portugoal.info | date=6 April 2013 | access-date=10 January 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150604002936/http://portugoal.info/index.php/more-liga-sagres-news/40396-boavista-back-in-the-top-flight | archive-date=4 June 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

The league was named Liga ZON Sagres until 2013–14 after the sponsorship agreement between Sagres, ZON (now NOS) and the league ended. The league is named Liga NOS since 5 February 2015.
